Task.Heading: Theorem 12.5.1.1 (Trace Formula), final comparison in its proof
Task.Question: For the tests and strip specified here, how does the author combine the two evaluations of the integral of the diagonal kernel to obtain the stated identity? Distinguish the algebraic implication from the analytic evaluations.

Source.anchor: Alessandro Maria Masullo, The Music of the Primes, https://math216.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/the-music-of-the-primes.pdf (SHA-256 e039d3f6cf0a4b14f03c7edb85097752dd65c0a2fe543c76fe992be234f97bf5), printed pp. 519–520 = PDF ordinals 519–520: Theorem 12.5.1.1 (Trace Formula), final comparison in its proof
Source.reading: Let \(L_{\mathrm{loc}}\) denote the three local sums on the left of (12.5.1.1)–(12.5.1.2). The first evaluation starts with the decomposition from (11.3.1.4): \(\int_{C_F}k_S(x,x)\,d\bar\mu(x)+\sum_{p\nmid S}\int_{C_F}k_p(x,x)\,d\bar\mu(x)=\int_{C_F}k(x,x)\,d\bar\mu(x)\). Theorem 11.3.2.1 makes each term in the sum vanish, and Theorem 12.4.1.1 evaluates the remaining \(k_S\) integral as \(L_{\mathrm{loc}}-\bigl[M(\varphi)(|\cdot|_F^{1/2})+M(\varphi)(|\cdot|_F^{-1/2})\bigr]\). The second evaluation, for \(I=[-\alpha,\alpha]\), is (12.5.1.4): \(\int_{C_F}k(x,x)\,d\bar\mu(x)=-\sum_{c,I}N(c)M(\varphi)(c|\cdot|_F^{-1/2})\). The final step is algebraic: equate these two values of the same integral and add the two Mellin terms to both sides. This gives the stated right-hand side (12.5.1.3), \(L_{\mathrm{loc}}=M(\varphi)(|\cdot|_F^{1/2})+M(\varphi)(|\cdot|_F^{-1/2})-\sum_{c,I}N(c)M(\varphi)(c|\cdot|_F^{-1/2})\).
Source.attribution: The author, in the proof of Theorem 12.5.1.1, invokes (11.3.1.4), Theorems 11.3.2.1 and 12.4.1.1, and, for (12.5.1.4), Definition 10.4.3.7 and Theorem 10.4.2.8.
Source.boundary: Theorem 12.5.1.1 (Trace Formula), final comparison in its proof: Both readings cover the final comparison of the proof ending at the QED box on p.520; supporting Theorems 11.3.2.1, 12.4.1.1, 10.4.2.8 and Def 10.4.3.7 are cited but not visible. Both correctly separate the algebraic step (equating the two values of ∫k(x,x) and transposing the subtracted Mellin pair) from the analytic inputs (vanishing of k_p integrals, k_S evaluation, (12.5.1.4)), under φ(C_F^1)=0, a=1/2, I=[-α,α]. The vanishing condition on p is faithfully rendered (first reading paraphrases the residue-characteristic condition; source says "not the prime residue characteristic of any finite place contained in S"). Both match the source's attribution and the strip/multiplicity definitions on p.519-520. Limited to this passage; the packet is not a proof and supplies no external realization assumptions.

Block: translate: mathlane candidate rejected: The packet fixes the signs and identifies the same global diagonal integral in both evaluations, but its source notes do not specify the common admissible test class. They give only the vanishing condition on C_F^1, a = 1/2, and I = [-alpha, alpha], without stating the test-function, support, or invariance hypotheses under which both evaluations apply. They also refer to the strip and multiplicity definitions without stating which c enter the sum or how N(c) is defined.
